newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The National Bureau of Statistics reported Wednesday that Koreans generally have no sex preference for the firt-born, but would prefer the second child to be male. The ratio in 1995 for female versus male newborns was 100:113.4.

- Kwon Young-kil, Chairman of the Korean Confederation of Trade Union announced Wednesday, that if the Labor Law was not repealed before the January 15, remaining public sector unions such as subway, Korea Telecom, and newspapers will join the nationwide strikes.

- A joint statement issued by the ministers of interior, justice, and labour on Wedneday urged workers who are on strike in protest at the recent enactment of a new labor law to stop their collective action and return to work or face "stern countermeasures".

- North Korea and the Korean Energy Development Organization (KEDO) officially clinched two agreements at 6.00 a.m. (2100 GMT Wednesday) this morning. This clears the way for construction of two 1,000 megawatt light-water reactors in Shinpo, North Korea. Nine more protocols remain to be signed, but the first five signed so far would give the go-ahead for the leveling of the ground at the site area, roads, and other infrastructure works.
